name: Mondscheinspitze
kurzbeschreibung: Rising to 2,106 metres in the Karwendel range, the striking Mondscheinspitze offers seasoned alpine hikers dramatic limestone ridges and stunning panoramas over Lake Achensee.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Mondscheinspitze (2,106 m) is one of the most distinctive and elegant peaks in the eastern Karwendel Alps. Situated west of Lake Achensee and north of the Gerntal valley, it forms the prominent cornerstone of the Montschein ridge, characterized by sheer limestone cliffs, jagged arêtes, and rugged glacial cirques. Its poetic name reflects the timeless allure of this alpine landmark. From the summit cross, hikers are rewarded with a breathtaking 360-degree panorama: to the east, the turquoise waters of Lake Achensee glisten brightly; to the south and west stretch the countless dramatic peaks of the Karwendel heartland, while the Bavarian Prealps rim the northern horizon. For experienced mountaineers, conquering this peak is widely regarded as a pinnacle adventure in the Achensee region.

Route & Anforderungen

Ascending the Mondscheinspitze is a classic, demanding mountain hike that requires excellent stamina to conquer approximately 1,100 metres of elevation gain and descent. The most popular trailhead begins at Gernalm in the idyllic Gerntal near Pertisau, ascending initially across lush alpine pastures to Plumsjoch and the welcoming Plumsjochhütte (1,630 m). Beyond the saddle, the route steepens markedly as it traverses rocky slopes towards the Schafjöchl ridge. The final summit push demands surefootedness and complete freedom from vertigo: navigating light scrambling terrain (UIAA grade I) involves short, wire-cable-secured rock passages. In wet conditions or when early-season snow patches linger, the limestone becomes exceptionally slippery, making dry weather essential.

Besuch & Anreise

The excursion begins in the village of Pertisau on the shores of Lake Achensee. A scenic toll road winds into the Gerntal valley up to the parking lot at the Gernalm mountain inn. Alternatively, hikers can approach from the Rißtal valley via the Plumsjochhütte. When using public transit, take the train to Jenbach railway station followed by regional buses to Pertisau, where summer hikers' shuttles operate into the Karwendel valleys.

Tipps

A stopover at the rustic Plumsjochhütte treats hikers to traditional Tyrolean cheese dumplings and grand views towards the Rißtal. Starting early in the morning greatly increases the likelihood of observing chamois and alpine marmots in the meadows below the peak. For a varied descent, consider completing a loop route via the scenic Schleimsjoch saddle.
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; mountain tours recommended from June to October
